display: I teach antenatal and postnatal yoga at a community centre in Stockport, and I have been running classes for about six years.

signals.text: I'm rewriting my antenatal handouts for the January term and want them checked by someone with clinical experience, such as a midwife or physio.
A partner told me one of my breathing tips differed from what their midwife said, so I'm going through every piece of advice I give and checking where it comes from.
I found three pieces of advice in my handouts that I picked up in training or from other teachers and can't source. I want to verify them or take them out.
I would like to run a mums-and-babies class on Friday mornings, but the centre has no second room and I haven't found anywhere else to hold it.
I'm capped at 14 women per class because of the room, and a waiting list would help me see if there is real demand.
The centre's room closes for a week in November for heating work. I need to tell participants early and may want somewhere else to hold that week's classes.
I have to confirm the January timetable by 30 November and am planning the spring term.
I'm training for the Manchester half marathon in April. My knees hurt on long runs and I'm looking for good advice on shoes and recovery.
I'm looking for a reliable, cheaper broadband provider in the Stockport area, as mine keeps dropping out.
I'm worn out and short of headspace this autumn because of things going on in my family.
A close relative has early dementia. I'm looking for practical guidance on care options and on how to talk to someone with memory loss.

offers.text: I can teach antenatal and postnatal yoga: breathing, pelvic floor work, positions for late pregnancy and gentle recovery after birth.
I have trained for 85 hours as a yoga teacher, plus a pregnancy specialism module, and I hold a current first aid certificate.
I hold regular classes in Stockport on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and Saturday mornings, with about 14 women per class.
I have a set of handouts on breathing, pelvic floor, late-pregnancy positions and postnatal recovery that I rewrite every term.
I have a mailing list of about 120 past and present participants, so I can reach local pregnant women and new mums directly.
I own bolsters, blocks, birth balls and a stack of mats, stored at the centre.
I'm good at guiding the final ten minutes of relaxation, which women tell me helps them rest and sometimes cry for the first time in weeks.
I can offer a guest session on breathing and relaxation for a midwife team, a baby group, a workplace or a parent-and-baby event during weekday daytimes.

catchers.hypo: I'm a community midwife. A colleague said you're looking for someone to check your breathing handouts, and I could read them over.
catchers.can: I can send over the breathing and positions handouts for a review before the January term, and then revise them according to the feedback.
catchers.confirm: Do you have recent clinical experience with antenatal women (for example as a midwife, doula with clinical training, or women's health physio)?

catchers.hypo: I'm a women's health physiotherapist and I'd like to give a short talk to local pregnancy classes about pelvic floor health.
catchers.can: I can host a guest talk or Q&A for my Stockport classes and share it with my mailing list.
catchers.confirm: Could you do the session on a weekday daytime or a Saturday morning, in or near Stockport?

catchers.hypo: I run a church hall, nursery or children's centre near Stockport that is empty on Friday mornings and I'd like to fill it with a mums-and-babies class.
catchers.can: I can run a Friday-morning mums-and-babies yoga class there and bring participants from my mailing list.
catchers.confirm: Is the room free on Friday mornings, with floor space for about 12 mats and babies?

catchers.hypo: I'm a new mum and I've just given birth. I'm anxious and tired, and I'd like a gentle class where I can bring my baby.
catchers.can: I can point her to my Saturday-morning postnatal class, which welcomes babies, or to the Friday class if I get a venue for it.
catchers.confirm: Do you live in or near Stockport and are you well enough for gentle movement (cleared by your GP or midwife)?

catchers.hypo: I work at a local business and we'd like to offer a short relaxation and breathing session for staff or for new parents.
catchers.can: I can lead a guided breathing and relaxation session during a weekday daytime.
catchers.confirm: Is this for a group of adults who can move on a mat, during a weekday between roughly 9am and 4pm?

catchers.hypo: I'm a runner and a yoga fan. I'd like to find a teacher who can show me stretches for runners' knees and recovery.
catchers.can: I can share simple stretches and mobility work from my own half-marathon training, or recommend a running partner via my club friend.
catchers.confirm: Is this general movement and stretching for fitness, not treatment for an injury?

catchers.hypo: I'm a dementia support worker in the Stockport area and I run a drop-in for families caring for someone with early dementia.
catchers.can: Through my family I can bring a relative (who lives ten minutes away) to the drop-in, and also pass the details on to my brother, who has to make decisions about care options.
catchers.confirm: Does your service support families in the first year after a diagnosis, and does it cover the Stockport area?

catchers.hypo: I'm a centre manager or community-venue coordinator and I'd like to know if you could run the same sessions at our venue.
catchers.can: I can run classes in other venues on weekday daytimes or Saturday mornings, as long as there is a room and a mat storage space.
catchers.confirm: Is there a room that suits quiet floor-based classes, with no fixed evening bookings that clash with Tuesday and Thursday?

forbids.text: I will not give medical advice, only movement and breathing guidance.
I won't present my own reading or experience as clinical fact. I want to be careful and honest about what I do and don't know.
Tuesday and Thursday evenings and Saturday mornings are taken by my classes.
I can't pay a professional rate for a review and would need someone willing to look at my handouts for free or for a small fee.
I'm not in a position to travel far from Stockport for classes or meetings.

projects.name: Clinically checked antenatal handouts
projects.text: I'm rewriting my breathing and positions handouts for the January term and want them reviewed by someone with clinical experience before then.
roles_needed: midwife or women's health physio reviewer

projects.name: Friday mums-and-babies class
projects.text: A new class for mums and babies on Friday mornings, which depends on finding a suitable room in Stockport.

policy.t1: When there is a real sign of a fit, I'll share what I'm working on: the handout review, the Friday class idea and my mailing list, with details of where I need help.
policy.t2: Once I know who you are and the fit is strong, I'll share what is going on in my family and what kind of support would help.
policy.never: I won't share my finances, my health worries or anything about my own medical risks.
